title: Routing That Is Identical in Dev and Prod — Check

questions.prompt: What does a Netlify redirect with status = 200 do?
questions.explanation: A 200 redirect is a rewrite/proxy: the browser still sees /agronomy-api/soil, but Netlify forwards the request internally to the target function.
options: Sends the browser a 301 to a new URL
Proxies (rewrites) the request internally while the browser keeps the original path

questions.prompt: What is the role of :splat in the redirect rule?
questions.explanation: :splat captures the wildcard portion of the path (e.g. soil?lat=36.7) and forwards it to the gateway function, preserving the route tail and query.
options: It captures whatever the * matched and passes it through to the function
It sets the HTTP status code
It selects the AI search endpoint

questions.prompt: Pointing the frontend at a localhost URL in dev and the real domain in prod via an environment variable fully preserves dev/prod parity.
questions.explanation: It breaks parity: dev and prod take different code paths and CORS behavior, so routing bugs can hide until deploy. Using a single relative path and varying only what answers it preserves parity.

questions.prompt: How does the gateway decide which domain module handles a request?
questions.explanation: The gateway dispatches on the path tail (e.g. 'soil') via a route table mapping names to domain functions, and both the prod rewrite and the local mock honor the same scheme.
options: By the path tail after /agronomy-api/, looked up in a route table
By the order functions are deployed
